ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — David Hume Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for three months of looser stools with dark blood, tiredness, and weight loss. Concerns: Three months of looser, more frequent stools with dark blood mixed in on several days, tiredness, and about 6 kg of unintended weight loss; Wants plain information about what is wrong and wants to keep working on his books through treatment. [S]

750 mg IV once a week for two doses

Four tablets twice daily on days 1 to 14 of each 21-day cycle

260 mg IV on day 1 every 21 days

One tablet every 8 hours as needed for nausea

As needed for diarrhea on capecitabine

tr.td: Colonoscopy to the cecum with biopsy: 4 cm ulcerated, partly circumferential, non-obstructing mass at 28 cm in the sigmoid colon, tattooed; no other lesions. Biopsy: moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, mismatch-repair proteins (MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6) intact
CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis with contrast: sigmoid wall thickening with two pericolic lymph nodes up to 7 mm; lungs clear; one 9 mm indeterminate low-density lesion in liver segment VI
MRI of the liver with contrast: the 9 mm segment VI lesion is a typical hemangioma, with peripheral nodular enhancement and progressive fill-in; no liver metastases

Laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy with primary anastomosis and no stoma. Pathology: adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, pT3 N1a (1 of 22 nodes), margins clear, no lymphovascular or perineural invasion; stage IIIB
Adjuvant CAPOX chemotherapy, four 21-day cycles (three months), given by medical oncology

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Colonoscopy with biopsy, CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, and baseline CEA for iron deficiency anemia with rectal bleeding in a man of 64
Medical oncology consultation to review staging, the indeterminate liver lesion, the order of treatment, and adjuvant therapy
Intravenous ferric carboxymaltose before surgery to correct iron deficiency anemia, with ferritin and blood count rechecked six to eight weeks later
Laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy with lymph node dissection by the colorectal surgery team
Three months (four cycles) of adjuvant CAPOX for low-risk stage III disease, after DPYD genotyping, with neuropathy, blood count, and diarrhea checks at every visit

Survivorship surveillance: history, examination, and CEA every 3 to 6 months for 2 years, then every 6 months to 5 years; CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis every 6 to 12 months for 5 years; colonoscopy one year after resection
Distress and depression screening at each visit, at least 150 minutes of activity a week, alcohol at or below one drink a day, and a written survivorship care plan
Complete diagnosis, staging, and curative resection within six weeks of presentation
Colonoscopy in eight days, staging complete in three and a half weeks, colectomy at five weeks
Replete iron stores before surgery and recover hemoglobin by the postoperative review
Ferritin 186 ng/mL and hemoglobin 12.4 g/dL four weeks after surgery, up from 9 ng/mL and 10.6 g/dL
Complete three months of adjuvant CAPOX with neuropathy no worse than grade 1
Four cycles completed on schedule; grade 1 sensory neuropathy
Start survivorship surveillance with a written survivorship care plan
Survivorship care plan given; CEA 1.8 ng/mL; CT and colonoscopy dates set
